niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want Jungian self-inquiry, a regular spiritual practice, or both. These are good starting points from the options I found:

### For shadow work
- **[Encounters with the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/course/encounters-with-the-shadow)** — A strong starting point for a Jungian approach, taught by Jungian analyst James Hollis. Best if you want depth-psychology concepts alongside reflection.
- **[Engage the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/courses)** — A broader collection of perspectives from multiple teachers, with material on shadow work in relationships and dreams. Check the catalog for the current course format and availability.
- **[Diving into the Shadow — Michael Lennox](https://michaellennox.com/classes/shadow/)** — A four-week online course; potentially a good fit if you prefer a time-bounded class.
- **[Shadow Work for Conscious Relationships — Jung Center of Chicago](https://jungchicago.org/product/shadow-work-for-conscious-relationships/)** — Especially relevant if you want to explore how shadow patterns show up in relationships.

### For spiritual practice
- **[Naropa University’s online learning courses](https://www.naropa.edu/academics/personal-enrichment/)** — Includes a free introductory mindfulness course, with Buddhist context and practices such as insight and calm abiding.
- **[Learn to Meditate — Meditation Mount](https://www.meditationmount.org/learn-to-meditate)** — A six-week online introduction to meditation.
- **[Contemplative Living I — Center for Theology and the Sciences](https://ctsnet.edu/events/contemplative-living-i-contemplative-practices-in-daily-life/)** — A longer, experiential course rooted in Christian contemplative practice; a better fit if that tradition resonates with you.

**My quick picks:** Start with *Encounters with the Shadow* for Jungian shadow work, and Naropa’s free mindfulness course for a low-commitment spiritual-practice foundation. If you want a course that explicitly combines shadow work and spirituality, look at Jung Platform’s broader catalog.

Course schedules, prices, and enrollment can change, so check each provider’s current details. Shadow work can bring up difficult emotions; choose a course that emphasizes pacing and support, and consider working with a qualified mental-health professional if you’re dealing with trauma or significant distress.
